name: Question 7
problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}0 & a & ∗ \\ 1 & b & ∗ \\ 0 & c & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices above. Given that $A=PJ{P}^{-1}$ is a Jordan canonical decomposition of $A,$ find the value of $2a+c.$
worked_solution:
Since the Jordan matrix $J$ has a single $3\times 3$ Jordan block corresponding to $\lambda =4,$ the columns of $P$ form the following chain: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3}\overset{A-4I\,}{\to }{v}_{2}\overset{A-4I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A-4I\,}{\to }0\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain that 

- the first column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ of the eigenvalue $\lambda =4,$

- the second column of $P$ corresponds to the vector ${v}_{2}$ such that $(A-4I){v}_{2}={v}_{1}.$

Now, computing $A-4I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-4I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the matrix equation $(A-4I){v}_{2}={v}_{1}$ is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we have ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
-{x}_{1}-2\cdot 0=1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-1.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get  

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $2a+c=2\cdot (-1)+0=-2.$

EXPLANATION

Since the Jordan matrix J has a single 3×3 Jordan block corresponding to λ=4, the columns of P form the following chain:

v3→A−4Iv2→A−4Iv1→A−4I0

As a result, we obtain that

  • the first column of P corresponds to the eigenvector v1=[010] of the eigenvalue λ=4,

  • the second column of P corresponds to the vector v2 such that (A−4I)v2=v1.

Now, computing A−4I, we get

A−4I=[40−1−142004]−4[100010001]=[00−1−10−2000].

So, the matrix equation (A−4I)v2=v1 is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[00−10−10−210000]R1↔R2∼[−10−2100−100000]

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the 1st and 3rd). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the second equation, we have x3=0. Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

−x1−2⋅0=1⟹x1=−1.

Hence, the general solution is

[−1x20],x2∈R.

Therefore, setting x2=1, we get

v2=[abc]=[−110].

Finally, 2a+c=2⋅(−1)+0=−2.
